takeaway: Dark blue-charcoal (#161923) + ivory text + one neon accent (#F40552); live player count next to the download CTA is the credibility engine; secondary CTA 'CREATE YOUR OWN SERVER' in spaced mono uppercase splits the audience in the hero.
Feature grid of flat square-cornered cards (icon + short claim) over a dimmed in-game screenshot; the whole page is one background with sections separated by density, not color bands.
Near-black + ivory wordmark + pink links and nothing else: extreme restraint is what makes a modding platform read as an institution, not a fan page.
Infrastructure legitimacy = enormous tight-tracked display type, monochrome UI, one geometric mark, and a partner-logo wall; color is almost absent so every accent means something.
Mono uppercase micro-labels in the utility bar + small line icons on flat feature cards give instant 'serious network product' credibility without any decoration.
Study, don't copy: keep its devices — '///' mono section labels (.NEWS.MODULE_HIGHLIGHT), trailing underscores, notched button corners — and drop its yellow/glitch identity entirely.
Nocturnal without pure black: a deep blue-violet field with subtle depth gradient feels like a place (community), where flat #000 feels like a void.
Night city is mostly deep blue-teal darkness (#02131a) punctuated by small saturated neon signs — neon is punctuation, never the field.
Server rack in the dark: near-black blue with one electric cyan LED glow (#01a9e7) — the exact 'quiet infrastructure, live signal' mood of the platform.
Dense monochrome circuit texture works as background material at very low contrast — technical depth without color noise.
